questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

This stove (had) a flat kerosene tank at the bottom.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **No improvement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​The original sentence, **"This stove had a flat kerosene tank at the bottom,"** is in the past tense and uses the verb **"had"** correctly.
 
• The use of** "had" **indicates that the stove possessed a flat kerosene tank in the past.
 
• Let's examine the options:
 
• **"have"**: This option changes the tense from past to present. However, the sentence is describing a specific stove in the past, so the present tense is not appropriate. 
 
• **"have had":** This option uses a present perfect tense, which indicates an action that started in the past and continues into the present. However, the sentence does not suggest an ongoing action; it simply describes the stove's feature in the past. Therefore, the present perfect tense is not suitable here. 
 
• **"has had":** This option uses a present perfect tense with the third-person singular subject "has." Similar to option 2, it suggests an ongoing action that does not align with the intended meaning of the sentence. The sentence refers to a specific stove in the past, so the present perfect tense is not appropriate. 
 
• **"no improvement": **This option states that no improvement is necessary, indicating that the original verb "had" is correct. Since the sentence correctly uses the past tense to describe the stove's feature in the past, no change is required. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** "no improvement" (option 4)** as the original sentence is already grammatically correct.

 

**Therefore, the correct sentence is ***This stove had a flat kerosene tank at the bottom.*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

She said, “Let us wait for the seat”

options.text: She proposed that they should wait for the seat.
She proposed that they could wait for the seat.
She proposed to wait for the seat.
She proposed let us wait for seat.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **She proposed that they should wait for the seat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• **'Let us'** shows a **suggestion**.
 
• In transition of speech, we use **should to express suggestion.**
 
• Let's look at the steps for changing the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
 
• The reporting verb 'said' is changed to 'proposed' because 'In Exclamatory sentences that express **(grief, sorrow, happiness, applaud)**, interjections are removed and the sentence is changed to an assertive sentence'.
 
• The pronoun 'us' is changed to 'they' as the first person changes according to subject.
 
• The conjunction 'that' is used in place of the comma and the inverted comma are removed.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct indirect speech will be** *She proposed that they should wait for the seat*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The following table will enable us to know how tense changes in indirect speech:-

 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Simple Present* (Subject + V1 + Object)*
 Simple Past* (Subject + V2 + Object)*
 
 

 Present Continuous *(Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Past Continuous *(Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)*
 
 

 Present Perfect *(Subject + has/have + V3 + Object)*
 Past Perfect* (Subject + had + V3 + Object)*
 
 

 Simple Past* (Subject + V2 + Object)*
 Past Perfect *(Subject + had + V3 + Object)*
 
 

 Past Continuous *(Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Past Perfect Continuous* (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object)*
 
 

 Simple Future *(Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object)*
 Present Conditional *(Subject + would + V1 +Object)*
 
 

 Future Continuous *(Subject + will/shall + V1 + ing + Object)*
 Conditional Continuous *(Subject + would + be + V1 + ing + Object)*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

One can achieve reward by hard work.

options.text: Reward could be achieved by hard work.
Reward is needed for hard work.
Reward is achieved by hard work.
Reward can be achieved by hard work.

questions.solution:
Here the correct sentence is **Reward can be achieved by hard work**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• Modals such as **can, should, might, could, may, will, shall, ought to*** *etc. are preserved during change of voice.
 
• Whenever a sentence in active voice contains a modal verb, it is changed according to the following structure:-
 
 
• Active Voice - **Modal verb + V₁**
 
• Passive Voice - **Modal verb + be + V3**
 
 
 
• **For Example:- **
 
 
• Active Voice - I **may** solve this sum.
 
• Passive Voice - This sum** may **be solved by me.
 
 
 
• Simple present (**achieve**) changes to simple past (**achieved**).
 
• The subject and object positions are interchanged.
 
• Since the subject of the active sentence is **'one' **i.e. **an indefinite subject**, it can be eliminated from the passive sentence.

**Therefore, the correct passive voice will be *** Reward can be achieved by hard work*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice,** three things need to be kept in mind**:-

 
 
• Change **object** into **subject**.
 
• Change **subject** into **object.**
 
• Always use **third form of verb** in passive voice.
 
• Use** 'by' **before the new object.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

He cooked (A)/ dinner and (B)/ than turned the radio on. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **C**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

 
• In the above given sentence, the error is in **part C**.
 
• It is so because **'than' **has been wrongly used in place of** 'then'**.
 
• **'Than' **is used for comparison *(more than; faster than, etc.)*
 
 
• For Example - She is younger than I am.
 
 
 
• **'Then' **is used to represent time. In the given context: **afterwards.**
 
 
• For Example - She said something and then rode ahead.
 
 
 
• Therefore,** 'than' **will be replaced by** 'then'**.

**Thus, the correct sentence is** *He cooked dinner and then turned the radio on*.
